All of Becky Lynch’s achievements and milestones throughout her career
In your reply, I’d like you to just list the results, nothing else.

entries.query:
All of Becky Lynch’s achievements and milestones throughout her career
In your reply, I’d like you to just list the results, nothing else.
entries.answer:
- SuperGirls Championship — 1 time; became the inaugural champion in 2005.
- SuperGirls Championship Tournament winner — 2005.
- World Queens of Chaos Championship — 1 time, won in 2006.
- Signed with WWE and joined NXT — 2013.
- WWE main-roster debut — 2015.
- Competed in the inaugural Women’s Royal Rumble — 2018.
- Competed in the first women’s Money in the Bank ladder match — 2017.
- Competed in WWE’s first women’s TLC match — TLC 2018.
- Competed in WWE’s first main-roster Last Woman Standing match — Evolution 2018.
- WWE SmackDown Women’s Championship / Women’s World Championship — 5 times, including becoming the **inaugural** SmackDown Women’s Champion at Backlash 2016.
- WWE Raw Women’s Championship — 2 times.
- WWE Women’s Intercontinental Championship — 3 times, the most in history.
- Longest individual WWE Women’s Intercontinental Championship reign — 163 days.
- Longest combined WWE Women’s Intercontinental Championship reign — record holder.
- WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship — 2 times: once with Lita and once with Lyra Valkyria.
- NXT Women’s Championship — 1 time.
- WWE Women’s Triple Crown Champion — WWE’s sixth woman to complete the Triple Crown.
- WWE Women’s Grand Slam Champion — WWE’s sixth woman to complete the Grand Slam.
- 2019 Women’s Royal Rumble winner.
- 2024 Women’s Elimination Chamber winner.
- First woman to win both the Raw Women’s Championship and SmackDown Women’s Championship simultaneously.
- Only WWE woman to have held the Raw and SmackDown women’s world titles at the same time.
- WrestleMania 35 main-event winner — defeated Ronda Rousey and Charlotte Flair to capture both women’s world championships.
- Took part in the first-ever women’s WrestleMania main event at WrestleMania 35.
- Pinned Ronda Rousey in that WrestleMania 35 main event.
- First European woman to win a WrestleMania main event.
- Seven-time WWE women’s world champion overall: five SmackDown/Women’s World title reigns and two Raw Women’s title reigns.
- Returned at WrestleMania 41 after nearly a year away and won the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Lyra Valkyria.
- WWE Year-End Award: Female Superstar of the Year — 2018 and 2019.
- WWE Year-End Award: Match of the Year — 2018, for her Last Woman Standing match against Charlotte Flair at Evolution.
- Pro Wrestling Illustrated Woman of the Year — 2018 and 2019.
- Ranked No. 1 in the PWI Women’s 100 — 2019.
- Pro Wrestling Illustrated Most Popular Wrestler — 2019.
- Sports Illustrated Women’s Wrestler of the Year — 2018 and 2019.
- Wrestling Observer Newsletter Women’s Wrestling MVP — 2018 and 2019.
- CBS Sports Wrestler of the Year — 2018.
- CBS Sports WWE Match of the Year — 2018, for the TLC match involving Asuka and Charlotte Flair.[1][2][3][4]
